UnitStatement: DEL-13-04 is named the Physical-to-analytical transformation contract.
DEL-13-04 belongs to package PKG-13, Physical Design Knowledge and Constraint Engine.
DEL-13-04 is a BACKEND_FEATURE_SLICE deliverable type.
DEL-13-04 covers scope item SOW-066.
DEL-13-04 supports objective OBJ-014.
The primary function of DEL-13-04 is to derive a solver-ready analytical model from the physical model.
The physical-to-analytical transformation is deterministic.
Transformation warnings are recorded when physical design data cannot be represented analytically.
Transformation traceability is part of OBJ-014 and DEL-13-04 decomposition context.
The physical source-of-truth model anchors editable design data.
The analytical model is a solver-ready idealization or analysis basis derived from the physical model.
The primary global analysis model target is a 3D centerline/frame model.
Unit-bearing physical values crossing boundaries require explicit unit metadata.
Missing solve-required values are explicit findings, not silent defaults.
Public artifacts must not bundle protected standards data, tables, or proprietary values.
Software must not claim certification, sealing, approval, authentication, or code compliance.
The transform implementation lives at core/model_transform/physical_to_analytical/contract.py.
The internal solver-boundary adapter lives at core/model_transform/physical_to_analytical/_solver_boundary_adapter.py.
The canonical physical fixture is fixtures/domain/invented_physical_source_of_truth_model.json.
TransformResult exposes analytical_model, diagnostics, traceability_links, and has_blocking_findings.
Default TransformSettings uses analytical_model_id = ANALYTICAL-DERIVED and contract_version = DEL-13-04-0.1.
The exact transform-loss taxonomy is TBD; implemented PTA-* and ASBA-* diagnostics are code/test evidence, not a final release taxonomy.
Exact dependency versions are TBD per the Architecture Basis Injection.
The local Dependencies.csv is an approved DAG-006 mirror/evidence surface listing ACTIVE upstream dependencies for DEL-13-04.
The physical-to-analytical transform starts from the canonical physical/domain model (DEL-02-01).
The transform consumes the design-knowledge schema (DEL-13-01).
The transform consumes constraint entities (DEL-13-02).
The transform consumes constraint validation (DEL-13-03).
The transform targets the 3D frame stiffness kernel model (DEL-04-01).
The transform needs support/boundary-condition modeling from linear support and restraint models (DEL-04-03).
The transform needs primitive load semantics from the primitive load case engine (DEL-05-01).
Engineering standards text is not locally available for this deliverable; clause-level requirements must not be derived.
PRD v0.2 is referenced by SOW-066 but not present locally; PRD-derived particulars remain TBD.
Public data policy forbids protected standards text, copied formulas, protected tables, protected examples, proprietary commercial data, or code-specific public defaults.
Deterministic mechanics tests are required before release; code-compliance acceptance remains outside software authority.
Transform consumption of DEL-13-02 beyond copied constraint_refs remains broader integration TBD.
Direct runtime validator invocation of DEL-13-03 by the transform remains TBD.
No GUI, runtime command, public API, or external prover workflow is implemented; these surfaces remain TBD.
Current analytical output carries empty analysis_run_refs, comparison_refs, handoff_package_refs, and external_reference_refs; persisted package and handoff readiness remain TBD.
The deliverable materialized as a provider-neutral Python transform contract, an internal solver-boundary DTO adapter, a canonical invented fixture, and focused tests.
The transform contract covers inputs, outputs, deterministic behavior, traceability, warning/diagnostic behavior, and unsupported-data handling for physical-to-analytical conversion.

The analytical model output is a derived analytical_solver_model with source_model_ref and centerline/frame arrays for nodes, elements, materials, sections, supports, and load cases, plus diagnostics, assumptions, and traceability links.

Deterministic PTA-* diagnostics cover missing source/model-role/coordinate data, missing fields, missing or TBD unit metadata, noncanonical dimensions, unsupported component/support/element data, and unresolved references.

The internal solver-boundary adapter provides a deterministic DTO boundary for nodes, straight-pipe connectivity, property bindings, support targets, load-case records/applications, adapter DTO identity/hash/source-chain records, and adapter diagnostics.

Traceability records include physical-to-analytical traceability_links plus adapter DTO source_chain, payload_hash_ref, result_trace_anchor, and solver_input_trace_anchor for emitted load applications.
Field-level scalar traceability and full runtime result trace-chain production remain TBD.

DEL-13-04 is the bridge from design authoring to solver execution, deriving a deterministic analytical_solver_model from a schema-shaped physical source-of-truth model while preserving diagnostics, omissions, assumptions, and traceability.
Treat the physical model as the editable source-of-truth and the analytical model as a derived view; do not overwrite physical design context during transformation.
The same physical input and contract configuration should yield the same analytical output and warning set.
When physical data cannot be represented analytically, expose the loss as a warning/diagnostic with traceability.
Unit-bearing values crossing the boundary need explicit unit metadata; missing or ambiguous units are findings.
Missing solve-required values must not be silently supplied.
Do not introduce protected code data, proprietary values, code-specific public defaults, SIF/flexibility tables, or compliance claims.
The default analytical target is the project's 3D centerline/frame mechanics boundary, not routine shell/solid FEA.

The transform emits deterministic PTA-* diagnostics for missing source/model-role/coordinate data, missing required fields, missing or TBD unit metadata, noncanonical quantity dimensions, unsupported components/supports/elements, and unresolved references.

The internal adapter emits deterministic ASBA-* diagnostics for missing properties, invalid y_reference, unsupported/noncanonical load semantics, unresolved targets, wrong dimensions, nonfinite quantities, unordered uniform-load spans, and wrong model role.
The final transform-loss taxonomy, release thresholds, and user-facing severity policy remain TBD until a governed decision accepts them.
Dependencies.csv rows are evidence of coordination dependencies, not permission to copy or reinterpret sibling deliverable content.

DEL-13-04 carries design_knowledge_refs and constraint_refs through the derived analytical model but does not invoke the validation engine, resolve owner criteria, or create a GUI/runtime/API integration path.
Implementation work should consume approved upstream contracts through explicit sealed scope and should not reclassify dependencies, expand schema vocabulary, or infer owner/code criteria.

Current transform diagnostics use classes such as SOLVE_BLOCKING, ASSUMPTION_WARNING, and NONLINEAR_WARNING; adapter diagnostics classify blocking findings as SOLVE_BLOCKING and other findings as diagnostic evidence only.
Transformation and adapter findings should be deterministic, source-linked, and reviewable, and must not state the model is compliant, professionally accepted, release-ready, or externally proven.

Public artifacts must not supply protected or proprietary values for component, material, section, support, load, constraint, or design-knowledge references; unknown or suspected protected sources require review/quarantine rather than normalization into public defaults.
Tests should use invented or permitted fixtures and should include provenance where data matters.
Preserve physical richness through traceability and warnings rather than forcing all data into solver elements.
Prefer explicit TBD, warning, or diagnostic records over hidden convenience defaults.

Specify behavior proven by SOW, decomposition, invariants, implementation, and tests; leave release taxonomy, external prover behavior, GUI/runtime/API integration, persistence/handoff readiness, and professional acceptance TBD.
Keep routine transformation aimed at 3D centerline/frame analysis and treat shell/solid FEA as a separate handoff path.
Executable invented examples are public-permissive test evidence, not owner/project or professional design examples; publication-grade and owner examples remain TBD.
PRD v0.2 Section 8.3 / FR-MOD-007 is not locally available, so PRD-specific transform clauses beyond SOW-066 wording remain TBD.
Broader upstream integration beyond current DEL-13-02/DEL-13-03 refresh evidence remains TBD until bounded implementation evidence exists.
OI-012 unresolved architecture detail means the transform-loss taxonomy cannot be finalized here and requires a later architecture/detail task.

The procedure defines a conservative workflow that keeps the physical model as source of truth, derives a solver-ready analytical representation, records transformation diagnostics, and preserves traceability without protected data, hidden defaults, API expansion, GUI/runtime behavior, external prover claims, or professional compliance claims.
Treat Dependencies.csv as the approved DAG-006 mirror/evidence surface; preserve approved rows as ACTIVE and do not retire, delete, or reclassify them during setup.
Use only source-cleared or invented/public-permissive data in examples and tests; suspected protected content must be quarantined and escalated.
Identify the physical model as the source-of-truth input.
Identify the analytical model as a derived solver-ready output with model_role = analytical_solver_model and source_model_ref pointing back to the physical model.
Confirm the default target mechanics boundary is the 3D centerline/frame model.

Supported physical-record coverage includes nodes, straight-pipe elements, supported component metadata referenced by valid elements, materials, sections, supports, load cases, combinations, diagnostics, unresolved assumptions, and traceability links.
Record broader physical-record coverage as TBD unless implementation/tests explicitly define its handling.
For each unit-bearing input, require explicit unit metadata unless the field is explicitly dimensionless.
For each input whose source, provenance, or units are missing, define a diagnostic/warning path instead of a silent default.

Schema-shaped contract fields include id, model_role, coordinate_system, nodes, elements, components, materials, sections, supports, load_cases, combinations, design_knowledge_refs, constraint_refs, diagnostics, unresolved_assumptions, and traceability_links.
Specify traceability links from physical inputs to analytical output records, warnings/diagnostics, omissions, assumptions, and unresolved TBD items.

The internal adapter specifies DTO outputs only as internal solver-boundary evidence: nodes, straight-pipe connectivity, property bindings, support targets, load-case records/applications, adapter DTO identity/hash/source-chain records, load-case diagnostics, and diagnostics.
Do not encode compliance, approval, certification, external-prover success, release readiness, or professional reliance status in transform or adapter outputs.
Define deterministic behavior in terms of equivalent input model, units, transform contract version, and configuration.
Adapter DTO hash evidence uses sha256 over sorted JSON payloads with JCS vocabulary where implemented.
Release-grade canonicalization and broader audit-manifest policy remain TBD unless fixed by a later governed decision.

Warning tests must include negative cases for missing solve-required physical input, physical data lacking a solver-ready analytical representation, and missing or ambiguous unit metadata on a unit-bearing value.
Mark uncertain protected content TBD or protected_suspected according to policy and escalate suspected protected content rather than normalizing it into public examples.
The internal adapter accepts only strict analytical_solver_model mappings and reports DTO/load/orientation/property failures as diagnostics.
Existing local dependency rows must remain unchanged during evidence refresh; historical row IDs remain audit evidence under the DAG-006 coordination basis.

Remaining TBD records include final transform-loss taxonomy, release thresholds, external prover behavior, GUI/runtime/API integration, persisted/handoff readiness, broader physical-record coverage, human acceptance, and professional/code-compliance boundaries.

DEL-13-04 specifies the backend contract for transforming the schema-backed physical model into a solver-ready analytical model and recording traceable transformation warnings when physical design data cannot be represented analytically.
In scope: a deterministic physical-to-analytical transformation contract for SOW-066.
In scope: warning/diagnostic behavior for omitted, unsupported, incomplete, or non-representable physical design data.
In scope: traceability from source physical model records to derived analytical model records, warnings, omissions, or assumptions.
In scope: contract-level tests for transformation warnings.

In scope: integration posture with architecture-basis constraints including Rust core/application services, schema-first command/query/job result envelopes, JSON Schema 2020-12 contracts, diagnostics/result envelopes, and deterministic tests.
Out of scope: protected standards data, code-specific defaults, protected tables, copied formulas, owner standards, proprietary catalog values, or private project data.
Out of scope: final engineering acceptance, code compliance, certification, sealing, approval, or professional reliance claims.
Out of scope: owner standards or final acceptance logic for physical design constraints, per PKG-13 package exclusions.

Out of scope: final transform-loss taxonomy, release thresholds, dependency versions, external prover behavior, GUI/runtime/API integration, persisted/handoff readiness, broader physical-record coverage, and human/professional acceptance.

contract.py implements transform_physical_to_analytical(...), TransformSettings, TransformResult, deterministic ordering, analytical_solver_model output, PTA-* diagnostics, and physical-to-analytical traceability links.

_solver_boundary_adapter.py implements the internal adapt_analytical_solver_model(...) DTO boundary emitting node DTOs, straight-pipe connectivity, property bindings, support targets, load-case records/applications, adapter DTO identity/hash/source-chain records, load_case_diagnostics, and adapter diagnostics.

invented_physical_source_of_truth_model.json is the canonical invented fixture with public-permissive nodes, a straight-pipe element, governed y_reference, material/section quantities, a support, strict load records, assumption/diagnostic evidence, and traceability.

The current evidence does not implement a GUI command path, runtime service envelope, public API, persistence/handoff package readiness, external prover behavior, full release threshold policy, or human/professional acceptance.
REQ-001: the contract shall transform the physical model into a solver-ready analytical model deterministically.
REQ-002: the contract shall record transformation warnings or diagnostics when physical design data cannot be represented analytically.
REQ-003: the contract shall preserve the physical model as the editable source-of-truth and produce the analytical model as a derived solver-oriented view.
REQ-004: the contract shall preserve traceability from physical source records to analytical records, omissions, assumptions, warnings, or other transform outcomes.
REQ-005: unit-bearing physical values crossing the transform boundary shall carry explicit unit metadata unless explicitly dimensionless.
REQ-006: missing solve-required values shall be represented as explicit findings and shall not be silently defaulted.
REQ-007: the analytical output shall target the project primary global mechanics boundary, a 3D centerline/frame model.
REQ-008: the contract shall not bundle protected standards content, code-specific default values, protected tables, copied formulas, proprietary catalog values, or owner standards.
REQ-009: the contract and its warnings shall not claim certification, sealing, approval, authentication, engineering acceptance, or code compliance.
REQ-010: solver-facing changes from this contract shall have deterministic verification tests before release.
REQ-011: the contract shall treat upstream dependency surfaces as prerequisite context and shall not reinterpret the local dependency mirror as independent dispatch authority.

REQ-012: the internal solver-boundary adapter shall accept only strict analytical_solver_model mappings and shall not become a public API, GUI/runtime path, external prover path, or final solver acceptance claim.
No external engineering standard text is locally available or authorized as source material for this deliverable.
Any requirement depending on PRD v0.2 Section 8.3 or FR-MOD-007 beyond SOW-066 text remains TBD because the PRD is not locally available.
Deterministic transform verification: same input and configuration produce equivalent analytical output and equivalent warnings/diagnostics, implemented in test_physical_to_analytical_transform.py.
Unit metadata verification: unit-bearing values are not accepted silently without explicit units, and no unit conversion is performed.
No-silent-defaults verification: missing solve-required physical data yields findings rather than inferred defaults.
